signals.title: USD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Trump Tariff Risk
signals.text: Trump's weekend threats regarding EU auto tariffs and retaliation against EU fines drive safe-haven USD demand against the G10 laggard CHF. This bilateral theme is underpinned by a massive +375bp OIS carry advantage for the USD and a restrictive +1.47% real rate vs CHF's accommodative -0.62%. The next Fed meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced) on 29 Jul is the catalyst for confirming this yield dominance.

signals.title: USD/JPY — JPY COT Short Squeeze Risk
signals.text: JPY COT net short -105.2k (28% long) creates significant squeeze risk if the 163.79 resistance fails, despite the +264bp OIS carry favoring USD. While the pair remains in a technical uptrend above all major SMAs, the positive JPY CESI (+10) suggests domestic data is outperforming, providing fundamental fuel for an unwind. The next BoJ meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced) on 31 Jul is the catalyst for resolving the carry vs. positioning conflict.

signals.title: EUR/USD — CESI Negative Divergence + Tariff Pressure
signals.text: EUR COT net short -74.6k and a deeply negative CESI (-43) signal persistent fundamental weakness as Trump tariff rhetoric targets the EU. The 1.1375 Friday close sits below all major SMAs, while the +144bp OIS carry advantage for USD further incentivizes the downside. The next Fed meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced) on 29 Jul is the catalyst for a potential break toward the 1.1200 handle.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Carry Support vs. Negative Data Flow
signals.text: AUD COT net long +21.9k (63% long) is vulnerable to a washout as AUD CESI (-14) highlights persistent data misses, keeping the pair stuck near 0.6983. The -73bp OIS carry advantage for AUD provides a structural floor, but the neutral retail bias suggests no immediate contrarian catalyst. The next RBA meeting (mkt: 21% hike priced) on 11 Aug determines if the current hike bias can withstand deteriorating economic surprises.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Positioning Crowding + Geopolitical Risk
signals.text: GBP COT net long +28.2k (64.8% long) creates downside risk as the pair trades below its SMA200 (1.34) following a 1.19% weekly decline. While the -11bp OIS carry is nearly neutral, upcoming shipping security talks in London and soft oil prices introduce idiosyncratic volatility. The next BoE meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced) on 30 Jul is the catalyst for confirming the current hold bias and clearing the long-positioning overhang.
